## Missing data

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/index/03-concept; notes-page: missing-data/index.qmd; note-sha256: 1aaffdef1ff35720c720bb2d581e4a977467bcc8589a4beb2bb53f78b37d8b96; role: concept -->

A missing-data analysis must state the unit, the measurement that should have been available, and the process that made an observed value unavailable.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Missingness is a relation among a linguistic unit, an intended measurement, and its realized record. A blank cell does not identify that relation by itself. A missing-data analysis must state the unit, the measurement that should have been available, and the process that made an observed value unavailable.

## Missing data

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/index/04-concept; notes-page: missing-data/index.qmd; note-sha256: 1aaffdef1ff35720c720bb2d581e4a977467bcc8589a4beb2bb53f78b37d8b96; role: concept -->

The first is the MIT-licensed Tanaka sentence collection in Jacy, whose Redwoods-style selection workflow is described by Tanaka et al. (2005) and Bond, Kuribayashi, and Hashimoto (2008).

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

This module develops that specification with two audited linguistic resources. The first is the MIT-licensed Tanaka sentence collection in Jacy, whose Redwoods-style selection workflow is described by Tanaka et al. (2005) and Bond, Kuribayashi, and Hashimoto (2008). Its outcome is availability of a grammar-generated, human-selected analysis. The second is the nonimputed release of Hillenbrand et al.'s (1995) vowel measurements, distributed in a permissioned repository. Its missing values are unavailable F2 or F3 measurements for recorded vowel tokens.

This distinction governs every method that follows.

These two absences have different meanings. An unselected Jacy item lacks an accepted result from a grammar-and-selection pipeline; it is not thereby a sentence without meaning. ## What counts as missing?

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/index/07-concept; notes-page: missing-data/index.qmd; note-sha256: 1aaffdef1ff35720c720bb2d581e4a977467bcc8589a4beb2bb53f78b37d8b96; role: concept -->

This is unit-level loss over time, not merely an empty acoustic cell.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

- **An absent record:** a speaker who was never recruited or a corpus token that was never sampled has no row. This is a sampling or coverage problem, not a missing cell in the realized table. - **Planned missingness:** a counterbalanced experiment may deliberately leave some participant--item combinations unpresented. Those omissions belong to the design; they are not accidental nonresponses. - **An undefined measure:** a word skipped on first pass has an observed skipping outcome, but no first-pass fixation duration. Reading studies consequently analyze skipping and fixation-contingent durations as distinct measures (Rayner et al. 2011). Coding the duration as `NA` does not create an unseen fixation duration. - **Measurement or analysis failure:** the record exists, but a value that the protocol intended to recover is unavailable. The Hillenbrand formant cells belong here, though the release does not identify a cell-specific cause. - **Dropout:** a participant begins a longitudinal or multi-session study but supplies no later records. This is unit-level loss over time, not merely an empty acoustic cell.

## From locations to assumptions

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/index/09-concept; notes-page: missing-data/index.qmd; note-sha256: 1aaffdef1ff35720c720bb2d581e4a977467bcc8589a4beb2bb53f78b37d8b96; role: concept -->

The labels MCAR, MAR, and MNAR are incomplete unless those variables and the unit of analysis are specified.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

We proceed in two steps. First, missingness patterns represent which intended values are observed. The indicator describes locations; it does not explain them. Second, missingness mechanisms state how the probability of observation may depend on named observed and unobserved variables. The labels MCAR, MAR, and MNAR are incomplete unless those variables and the unit of analysis are specified.

## From locations to assumptions

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/index/10-concept; notes-page: missing-data/index.qmd; note-sha256: 1aaffdef1ff35720c720bb2d581e4a977467bcc8589a4beb2bb53f78b37d8b96; role: concept -->

The mechanism is an assumption about the process that produced that pattern.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

This distinction parallels the separation between a sampling design and an outcome model. The pattern is observed data. The mechanism is an assumption about the process that produced that pattern.

## Deletion, reconstruction, and checking

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/index/11-concept; notes-page: missing-data/index.qmd; note-sha256: 1aaffdef1ff35720c720bb2d581e4a977467bcc8589a4beb2bb53f78b37d8b96; role: concept -->

If selection depends on the response or a predictor, the retained rows may describe a different population from the eligible rows.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Complete-case analysis retains rows observed on every variable required by a particular analysis. It thus defines a selection indicator. If selection depends on the response or a predictor, the retained rows may describe a different population from the eligible rows.

## Deletion, reconstruction, and checking

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/index/12-concept; notes-page: missing-data/index.qmd; note-sha256: 1aaffdef1ff35720c720bb2d581e4a977467bcc8589a4beb2bb53f78b37d8b96; role: concept -->

It is not a recovered observation, and a single completed matrix does not propagate uncertainty about the prediction.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Iterative PCA imputation takes a different route. It uses the rank-$K$ reconstruction of a completed matrix to update its missing cells while returning observed cells to their measured values. The resulting number is a model-based prediction under a low-rank assumption. It is not a recovered observation, and a single completed matrix does not propagate uncertainty about the prediction.

## Deletion, reconstruction, and checking

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/index/13-concept; notes-page: missing-data/index.qmd; note-sha256: 1aaffdef1ff35720c720bb2d581e4a977467bcc8589a4beb2bb53f78b37d8b96; role: concept -->

It can reveal reconstruction failures under the tested masks, but it cannot reveal the values that were naturally missing.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Finally, validation by artificial masking hides some observed values, fits the full procedure without them, and compares the held-out reconstructions with their known values. This extends the earlier distinction between training and test data to matrix cells. It can reveal reconstruction failures under the tested masks, but it cannot reveal the values that were naturally missing.

## Deletion, reconstruction, and checking

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/index/14-concept; notes-page: missing-data/index.qmd; note-sha256: 1aaffdef1ff35720c720bb2d581e4a977467bcc8589a4beb2bb53f78b37d8b96; role: concept -->

A blank becomes statistically interpretable only after we name its unit, variable, and observation process.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The order of the module follows the decisions an analysis requires: (i) specify what should have been observed, (ii) describe where it is absent, (iii) state assumptions about why, (iv) make deletion explicit, (v) define one reconstruction method, and (vi) test that method under registered artificial masks. A blank becomes statistically interpretable only after we name its unit, variable, and observation process.

## Missingness patterns

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-patterns/02-concept; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-patterns.qmd; note-sha256: 0d19622aa3532c7f60a4f83467b2fdabcdb83fd2e6ce20b5b4a533bfec0d11e6; role: concept -->

In the Redwoods-style workflow described by Tanaka et al. (2005), the Jacy grammar generates analyses for a Japanese sentence and a human annotator selects among them using discriminants.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The Tanaka corpus provides a useful first case because its absences arise inside a linguistic analysis pipeline, not from an invented table. In the Redwoods-style workflow described by Tanaka et al. (2005), the Jacy grammar generates analyses for a Japanese sentence and a human annotator selects among them using discriminants. Bond, Kuribayashi, and Hashimoto (2008) describe the Tanaka annotation cycle. A selected analysis carries a grammar-derived Minimal Recursion Semantics (MRS) representation; its predicates and links are thus not separate hand annotations.

## From a binary indicator to three observed states {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-patterns/05-math; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-patterns.qmd; note-sha256: 0d19622aa3532c7f60a4f83467b2fdabcdb83fd2e6ce20b5b4a533bfec0d11e6; role: math -->

Let $Y_i$ denote a downstream quantity calculated from the selected MRS for item $i$. Its availability indicator is

$$
R_i=
\begin{cases}
1 & \text{if at least one analysis was selected},\\
0 & \text{if no analysis was selected}.
\end{cases}
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Let $Y_i$ denote a downstream quantity calculated from the selected MRS for item $i$. Its availability indicator is

$$
R_i=
\begin{cases}
1 & \text{if at least one analysis was selected},\\
0 & \text{if no analysis was selected}.
\end{cases}
$$

## From a binary indicator to three observed states {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-patterns/06-math; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-patterns.qmd; note-sha256: 0d19622aa3532c7f60a4f83467b2fdabcdb83fd2e6ce20b5b4a533bfec0d11e6; role: math -->

We therefore define a three-state categorical variable:

$$
C_i=
\begin{cases}
\text{selected analysis} & \text{if a preference record exists},\\
\text{parsed, unselected} & \text{if positive readings exist but none was selected},\\
\text{no positive reading} & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The binary indicator records whether $Y_i$ is available, but it merges two observed pipeline outcomes. Some unselected items have positive parse readings, while others have no positive reading recorded. We therefore define a three-state categorical variable:

$$
C_i=
\begin{cases}
\text{selected analysis} & \text{if a preference record exists},\\
\text{parsed, unselected} & \text{if positive readings exist but none was selected},\\
\text{no positive reading} & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

[Sources]

https://aclanthology.org/P05-1041/
https://www.anlp.jp/proceedings/annual_meeting/2008/pdf_dir/PC1-7.pdf
https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/~aac10/papers/mrs.pdf

## A pattern does not identify its mechanism

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-patterns/12-concept; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-patterns.qmd; note-sha256: 0d19622aa3532c7f60a4f83467b2fdabcdb83fd2e6ce20b5b4a533bfec0d11e6; role: concept -->

The profile differences above may challenge a description in which selected analyses are equally available everywhere, but they cannot establish why selection varies.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

A missingness pattern is observed data. A missingness mechanism is an assumption about the process that produced it. The profile differences above may challenge a description in which selected analyses are equally available everywhere, but they cannot establish why selection varies.

## Missingness mechanisms

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms/02-concept; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms.qmd; note-sha256: 0b735f7eee6d0eb11a070eb18f7a9fa00f96372149673595f097c1fd9bf01f21; role: concept -->

It is not yet a diagnosis of why an analysis is unavailable.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The preceding page distinguished selected analyses, parsed but unselected items, and items with no positive reading. We now ask whether the binary outcome $S_i=1$ for a selected analysis is associated with two measurements observed for every profile item: its profile and its released token count. This is a descriptive question about the pinned release. It is not yet a diagnosis of why an analysis is unavailable.

[Sources]

https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-abstract/63/3/581/270932
:::

## Missingness mechanisms

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms/03-concept; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms.qmd; note-sha256: 0b735f7eee6d0eb11a070eb18f7a9fa00f96372149673595f097c1fd9bf01f21; role: concept -->

They do not name three visual arrangements of blank cells.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

A **missingness mechanism** states how an observation probability depends on observed and unobserved quantities. The three standard mechanisms make different conditional-dependence claims. They do not name three visual arrangements of blank cells.

[Sources]

https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-abstract/63/3/581/270932
:::

## Separating observed and unobserved quantities {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms/04-math; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms.qmd; note-sha256: 0b735f7eee6d0eb11a070eb18f7a9fa00f96372149673595f097c1fd9bf01f21; role: math -->

Let $Y_i$ be an intended measurement that is unavailable when $R_i=0$, and let $X_i$ collect quantities observed regardless of availability. The observation mechanism concerns

$$
\mathbb{P}(R_i=1\mid X_i,Y_i).
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Let $Y_i$ be an intended measurement that is unavailable when $R_i=0$, and let $X_i$ collect quantities observed regardless of availability. The observation mechanism concerns

$$
\mathbb{P}(R_i=1\mid X_i,Y_i).
$$

[Sources]

https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-abstract/63/3/581/270932
:::

## Separating observed and unobserved quantities

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms/05-concept; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms.qmd; note-sha256: 0b735f7eee6d0eb11a070eb18f7a9fa00f96372149673595f097c1fd9bf01f21; role: concept -->

The labels MCAR, MAR, and MNAR restrict which named quantities that probability may depend on.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The labels MCAR, MAR, and MNAR restrict which named quantities that probability may depend on.

[Sources]

https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-abstract/63/3/581/270932
:::

## Separating observed and unobserved quantities {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms/06-math; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms.qmd; note-sha256: 0b735f7eee6d0eb11a070eb18f7a9fa00f96372149673595f097c1fd9bf01f21; role: math -->

Values are **missing completely at random (MCAR)** when the observation probability depends on neither the observed covariates nor the unobserved measurement:

$$
\mathbb{P}(R_i=1\mid X_i,Y_i)=\mathbb{P}(R_i=1).
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Values are **missing completely at random (MCAR)** when the observation probability depends on neither the observed covariates nor the unobserved measurement:

$$
\mathbb{P}(R_i=1\mid X_i,Y_i)=\mathbb{P}(R_i=1).
$$

[Sources]

https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-abstract/63/3/581/270932
:::

## Separating observed and unobserved quantities

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms/07-concept; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms.qmd; note-sha256: 0b735f7eee6d0eb11a070eb18f7a9fa00f96372149673595f097c1fd9bf01f21; role: concept -->

Failure to find a visible association would not establish MCAR, because a finite dataset contains no direct information about the missing $Y_i$ values.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Under this account, observed rows form a random subset with respect to the variables in the statement. Failure to find a visible association would not establish MCAR, because a finite dataset contains no direct information about the missing $Y_i$ values.

[Sources]

https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-abstract/63/3/581/270932
:::

## Separating observed and unobserved quantities {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms/08-math; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms.qmd; note-sha256: 0b735f7eee6d0eb11a070eb18f7a9fa00f96372149673595f097c1fd9bf01f21; role: math -->

Values are **missing at random (MAR)** when observation may depend on observed measurements but does not additionally depend on the unavailable value after conditioning on them:

$$
\mathbb{P}(R_i=1\mid X_i,Y_i)=\mathbb{P}(R_i=1\mid X_i).
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Values are **missing at random (MAR)** when observation may depend on observed measurements but does not additionally depend on the unavailable value after conditioning on them:

$$
\mathbb{P}(R_i=1\mid X_i,Y_i)=\mathbb{P}(R_i=1\mid X_i).
$$

[Sources]

https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-abstract/63/3/581/270932
:::

## Separating observed and unobserved quantities

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms/09-concept; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms.qmd; note-sha256: 0b735f7eee6d0eb11a070eb18f7a9fa00f96372149673595f097c1fd9bf01f21; role: concept -->

The claim is conditional: once the stated $X_i$ is held fixed, $Y_i$ supplies no further information about observation.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

MAR may thus produce systematic, visible missingness. The claim is conditional: once the stated $X_i$ is held fixed, $Y_i$ supplies no further information about observation.

[Sources]

https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-abstract/63/3/581/270932
:::

## Separating observed and unobserved quantities {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms/10-math; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms.qmd; note-sha256: 0b735f7eee6d0eb11a070eb18f7a9fa00f96372149673595f097c1fd9bf01f21; role: math -->

Values are **missing not at random (MNAR)** when observation still depends on the unavailable value after the observed quantities have been considered:

$$
\mathbb{P}(R_i=1\mid X_i,Y_i)
\neq \mathbb{P}(R_i=1\mid X_i).
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Values are **missing not at random (MNAR)** when observation still depends on the unavailable value after the observed quantities have been considered:

$$
\mathbb{P}(R_i=1\mid X_i,Y_i)
\neq \mathbb{P}(R_i=1\mid X_i).
$$

[Sources]

https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-abstract/63/3/581/270932
:::

## Separating observed and unobserved quantities

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms/11-concept; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms.qmd; note-sha256: 0b735f7eee6d0eb11a070eb18f7a9fa00f96372149673595f097c1fd9bf01f21; role: concept -->

Domain knowledge about the data-producing process and sensitivity analyses are needed to study plausible MNAR departures.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The observed data generally do not identify this residual dependence. Domain knowledge about the data-producing process and sensitivity analyses are needed to study plausible MNAR departures.

[Sources]

https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-abstract/63/3/581/270932
:::

## Loading the Jacy availability outcome {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms/13-math; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms.qmd; note-sha256: 0b735f7eee6d0eb11a070eb18f7a9fa00f96372149673595f097c1fd9bf01f21; role: math -->

The descriptive model is

$$
S_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_i),
\qquad
\operatorname{logit}(\pi_i)
=\alpha+\beta_1L_i+\beta_2L_i^2+\gamma_{P_i}.
$$

They do not turn token count into a causal explanation.

These quantities summarize an association in this release.

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms/16-concept; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms.qmd; note-sha256: 0b735f7eee6d0eb11a070eb18f7a9fa00f96372149673595f097c1fd9bf01f21; role: concept -->

## Why the association does not classify the mechanism

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms/19-concept; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms.qmd; note-sha256: 0b735f7eee6d0eb11a070eb18f7a9fa00f96372149673595f097c1fd9bf01f21; role: concept -->

A mechanism label is meaningful only after the missing quantity and target population have been specified.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

If a downstream MRS property is the intended $Y_i$, selection is its availability indicator. But for an item with no acceptable grammar analysis, the counterfactual value of that property may itself require a more precise definition. Thus a mechanism label is meaningful only after the missing quantity and target population have been specified.

[Sources]

https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-abstract/63/3/581/270932
:::

## Why the association does not classify the mechanism

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms/20-concept; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms.qmd; note-sha256: 0b735f7eee6d0eb11a070eb18f7a9fa00f96372149673595f097c1fd9bf01f21; role: concept -->

The model cannot adjudicate among these accounts.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Even under such a specification, the plot contains $S_i$, profile, and length, not the unavailable $Y_i$. The association is compatible with an MAR account based on observed pipeline covariates. It is also compatible with an MNAR account involving properties of an unavailable acceptable analysis. And profile or length may stand in for unrecorded stages of parsing and annotation. The model cannot adjudicate among these accounts.

[Sources]

https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-abstract/63/3/581/270932
:::

## Why the association does not classify the mechanism

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms/21-concept; notes-page: missing-data/missingness-mechanisms.qmd; note-sha256: 0b735f7eee6d0eb11a070eb18f7a9fa00f96372149673595f097c1fd9bf01f21; role: concept -->

Treating all three as the same blank would merge a coverage problem with two observed pipeline states.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Mechanisms can also differ by level. A sentence outside the corpus has no profile row; a profile item with no positive reading has a row but no positive parse; and a parsed item may remain unselected. Treating all three as the same blank would merge a coverage problem with two observed pipeline states.

[Sources]

https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-abstract/63/3/581/270932
:::

## Defining the analysis set {.equation-slide .compact}

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/complete-case-analysis/05-math; notes-page: missing-data/complete-case-analysis.qmd; note-sha256: 0f528448ce6323dbf3aa0eb9bc50b9b454986831ec9f06c7b46544442d5fe9cb; role: math -->

**Complete-case analysis**, also called listwise deletion, retains only rows observed on every variable required by an analysis. Let $J$ be that set of variables. For token $i$,

$$
C_i=\prod_{j\in J}R_{ij}.
$$

Because each $R_{ij}$ is zero or one, $C_i=1$ only when every required value is observed.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

**Complete-case analysis**, also called listwise deletion, retains only rows observed on every variable required by an analysis. Let $J$ be that set of variables. For token $i$,

$$
C_i=\prod_{j\in J}R_{ij}.
$$

Because each $R_{ij}$ is zero or one, $C_i=1$ only when every required value is observed.

[Sources]

https://doi.org/10.1121/1.411872
https://github.com/santiagobarreda/hillenbrand_et_al_1995/tree/6dd44decc8ef5b537cbb54732a3b00c8fa652e65

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/complete-case-analysis/06-math; notes-page: missing-data/complete-case-analysis.qmd; note-sha256: 0f528448ce6323dbf3aa0eb9bc50b9b454986831ec9f06c7b46544442d5fe9cb; role: math -->

A complete-case estimate of a mean is

$$
\bar Y_{C=1}
=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}C_iY_i}{\sum_{i=1}^{n}C_i}.
$$

## Which steady measurements are absent?

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/complete-case-analysis/10-concept; notes-page: missing-data/complete-case-analysis.qmd; note-sha256: 0f528448ce6323dbf3aa0eb9bc50b9b454986831ec9f06c7b46544442d5fe9cb; role: concept -->

The 51 incomplete tokens are the union of two disjoint patterns in this five-variable analysis.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Duration, F0, and steady F1 are observed for every token. 10 tokens lack steady F2 while retaining steady F3; 41 lack steady F3 while retaining steady F2; none lacks both. Thus the 51 incomplete tokens are the union of two disjoint patterns in this five-variable analysis.

## Several columns determine joint retention {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/complete-case-analysis/16-math; notes-page: missing-data/complete-case-analysis.qmd; note-sha256: 0f528448ce6323dbf3aa0eb9bc50b9b454986831ec9f06c7b46544442d5fe9cb; role: math -->

Even high marginal availability does not determine the complete-case rate. In general,

$$
\mathbb{P}(C_i=1)
=\mathbb{P}\left(\bigcap_{j\in J}\{R_{ij}=1\}\right).
$$

$$

=\mathbb{P}\left(\bigcap_{j\in J}\{R_{ij}=1\}\right).

## When does deletion preserve a target?

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/complete-case-analysis/19-concept; notes-page: missing-data/complete-case-analysis.qmd; note-sha256: 0f528448ce6323dbf3aa0eb9bc50b9b454986831ec9f06c7b46544442d5fe9cb; role: concept -->

If formant availability depends on observed duration or vowel and these variables are related to the estimand, unadjusted deletion may change the relevant distribution.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Under MCAR with respect to the variables in a stated analysis, complete rows form a random subset, so familiar complete-case estimates may preserve their full-data targets. MAR does not provide this guarantee automatically. If formant availability depends on observed duration or vowel and these variables are related to the estimand, unadjusted deletion may change the relevant distribution.

[Sources]

https://doi.org/10.1121/1.411872
https://github.com/santiagobarreda/hillenbrand_et_al_1995/tree/6dd44decc8ef5b537cbb54732a3b00c8fa652e65
https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/sec-MCAR.html
:::

## When does deletion preserve a target?

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/complete-case-analysis/20-concept; notes-page: missing-data/complete-case-analysis.qmd; note-sha256: 0f528448ce6323dbf3aa0eb9bc50b9b454986831ec9f06c7b46544442d5fe9cb; role: concept -->

A report should state which variables define $J$, how many rows remain, and which complete-row population the estimate describes.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The condition also depends on the estimand. Missingness in a response and missingness in a predictor do not have identical consequences for every estimate. Thus a report should state which variables define $J$, how many rows remain, and which complete-row population the estimate describes.

https://github.com/santiagobarreda/hillenbrand_et_al_1995/tree/6dd44decc8ef5b537cbb54732a3b00c8fa652e65
https://stefvanbuuren.name/fimd/sec-MCAR.html
:::

## Iterative PCA imputation

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/pca-imputation/02-concept; notes-page: missing-data/pca-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 7bd37664d6f3a026b10ce8d75b68f49a60f96d3f581fffb2b2dc5bddc0b2b8c2; role: concept -->

The result is a prediction of a released acoustic cell, not a recovered observation from the recording.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The complete-case analysis discarded a Hillenbrand token whenever one of five steady measurements was unavailable. We now retain the tokens and ask whether the other acoustic measurements predict an unavailable formant estimate. The result is a prediction of a released acoustic cell, not a recovered observation from the recording.

[Sources]

https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/missMDA/html/imputePCA.html

Principal components and matrix reconstruction have already been introduced; the new object is the update procedure.

## Defining the standardized update {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/pca-imputation/07-math; notes-page: missing-data/pca-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 7bd37664d6f3a026b10ce8d75b68f49a60f96d3f581fffb2b2dc5bddc0b2b8c2; role: math -->

Each fit estimates a center $\widehat\mu_j$ and scale $\widehat s_j$ from its observed training cells, then forms

$$
Z_{ij}=\frac{Y_{ij}-\widehat\mu_j}{\widehat s_j}
$$

where $Y_{ij}$ is available.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Let $\mathbf{Y}$ be the incomplete acoustic matrix and let $M$ contain the cells treated as missing in a particular fit. Each fit estimates a center $\widehat\mu_j$ and scale $\widehat s_j$ from its observed training cells, then forms

$$
Z_{ij}=\frac{Y_{ij}-\widehat\mu_j}{\widehat s_j}
$$

where $Y_{ij}$ is available.

[Sources]

https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/missMDA/html/imputePCA.html
:::

## Defining the standardized update {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/pca-imputation/08-math; notes-page: missing-data/pca-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 7bd37664d6f3a026b10ce8d75b68f49a60f96d3f581fffb2b2dc5bddc0b2b8c2; role: math -->

Missing standardized cells begin at zero, which is the training-column mean after standardization. At iteration $t$, the rank-$K$ reconstruction is

$$
\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(t)}_K
=\mathbf U^{(t)}_K\mathbf D^{(t)}_K
\mathbf V_K^{(t)\mathsf T}.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Missing standardized cells begin at zero, which is the training-column mean after standardization. At iteration $t$, the rank-$K$ reconstruction is

$$
\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{(t)}_K
=\mathbf U^{(t)}_K\mathbf D^{(t)}_K
\mathbf V_K^{(t)\mathsf T}.
$$

[Sources]

https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/missMDA/html/imputePCA.html
:::

## Defining the standardized update {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/pca-imputation/09-math; notes-page: missing-data/pca-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 7bd37664d6f3a026b10ce8d75b68f49a60f96d3f581fffb2b2dc5bddc0b2b8c2; role: math -->

One update is

$$
Z_{ij}^{(t+1)}=
\begin{cases}
Z_{ij} & \text{if }(i,j)\notin M,\\
\widehat Z_{K,ij}^{(t)} & \text{if }(i,j)\in M.
\end{cases}
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

One update is

$$
Z_{ij}^{(t+1)}=
\begin{cases}
Z_{ij} & \text{if }(i,j)\notin M,\\
\widehat Z_{K,ij}^{(t)} & \text{if }(i,j)\in M.
\end{cases}
$$

[Sources]

https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/missMDA/html/imputePCA.html
:::

## Defining the standardized update {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/pca-imputation/10-math; notes-page: missing-data/pca-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 7bd37664d6f3a026b10ce8d75b68f49a60f96d3f581fffb2b2dc5bddc0b2b8c2; role: math -->

Thus only the missing cells change. We stop when their relative squared change is below $10^{-6}$,

$$
\frac{
  \sum_{(i,j)\in M}
  \left(Z_{ij}^{(t+1)}-Z_{ij}^{(t)}\right)^2
}{
  \sum_{(i,j)\in M}\left(Z_{ij}^{(t)}\right)^2
}<10^{-6},
$$

or after 1,000 iterations.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Thus only the missing cells change. We stop when their relative squared change is below $10^{-6}$,

$$
\frac{
  \sum_{(i,j)\in M}
  \left(Z_{ij}^{(t+1)}-Z_{ij}^{(t)}\right)^2
}{
  \sum_{(i,j)\in M}\left(Z_{ij}^{(t)}\right)^2
}<10^{-6},
$$

or after 1,000 iterations.

[Sources]

https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/missMDA/html/imputePCA.html
:::

## Imputed values remain estimates

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/pca-imputation/19-concept; notes-page: missing-data/pca-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 7bd37664d6f3a026b10ce8d75b68f49a60f96d3f581fffb2b2dc5bddc0b2b8c2; role: concept -->

An imputed cell contains a prediction under a linear low-rank assumption, training centers and scales, the selected rank, and an initialization rule.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

A completed matrix may look indistinguishable from an observed matrix in software. The two kinds of cells are not epistemically equivalent. An observed cell contains an estimate obtained from the recorded signal. An imputed cell contains a prediction under a linear low-rank assumption, training centers and scales, the selected rank, and an initialization rule.

[Sources]

https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/missMDA/html/imputePCA.html
:::

## Imputed values remain estimates

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/pca-imputation/20-concept; notes-page: missing-data/pca-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 7bd37664d6f3a026b10ce8d75b68f49a60f96d3f581fffb2b2dc5bddc0b2b8c2; role: concept -->

The completed data should thus retain the observation indicator.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Using one completed matrix in a later analysis treats these predictions as fixed and may understate the uncertainty created by the missing measurements. A procedure that propagates imputation uncertainty requires more machinery than this single reconstruction. The completed data should thus retain the observation indicator.

[Sources]

https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/missMDA/html/imputePCA.html
:::

## Imputed values remain estimates

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/pca-imputation/21-concept; notes-page: missing-data/pca-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 7bd37664d6f3a026b10ce8d75b68f49a60f96d3f581fffb2b2dc5bddc0b2b8c2; role: concept -->

Numerical convergence diagnoses the update, not the substantive adequacy of the low-rank representation.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

PCA imputation may also pull unusual but real measurements toward the leading linear components. A rare vowel category, a nonlinear acoustic relation, or an extreme value can be reconstructed poorly even when the algorithm converges. Numerical convergence diagnoses the update, not the substantive adequacy of the low-rank representation.

[Sources]

https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/missMDA/html/imputePCA.html
:::

https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/missMDA/html/imputePCA.html

## Checking the reconstruction

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/pca-imputation/26-concept; notes-page: missing-data/pca-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 7bd37664d6f3a026b10ce8d75b68f49a60f96d3f581fffb2b2dc5bddc0b2b8c2; role: concept -->

We next test that selected procedure by masking values that were actually observed.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Iterative PCA imputation alternates between rank-$K$ reconstruction and replacement of cells treated as missing. It preserves observed cells, but its predictions depend on a low-rank model and a validation-selected component count. We next test that selected procedure by masking values that were actually observed.

## Validating an imputation procedure

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/validating-imputation/02-concept; notes-page: missing-data/validating-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 57849066c62bd1fc5bd2959576cc380cafa4b3815fa7b03af158d050a6b793db; role: concept -->

We can ask a narrower question: when an available F2 or F3 estimate is hidden on purpose, how accurately does the complete procedure reconstruct it?

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The values of the naturally missing Hillenbrand formant cells are unavailable. No direct error can compare their PCA predictions with unseen measurements. We can ask a narrower question: when an available F2 or F3 estimate is hidden on purpose, how accurately does the complete procedure reconstruct it?

## Validating an imputation procedure

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/validating-imputation/03-concept; notes-page: missing-data/validating-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 57849066c62bd1fc5bd2959576cc380cafa4b3815fa7b03af158d050a6b793db; role: concept -->

The masking creates known targets while preserving the rule that a target cannot guide its own prediction.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

**Holdout validation by artificial masking** turns observed cells into artificial missing cells, fits the imputation without those values, and compares their reconstructions with the values set aside. This applies training and test separation to matrix cells. The masking creates known targets while preserving the rule that a target cannot guide its own prediction.

[Sources]

Course note: missing-data/validating-imputation.qmd
:::

## Defining the validation error {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/validating-imputation/04-math; notes-page: missing-data/validating-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 57849066c62bd1fc5bd2959576cc380cafa4b3815fa7b03af158d050a6b793db; role: math -->

Its mean squared reconstruction error is

$$
\operatorname{MSE}(M_r)
=\frac{1}{|M_r|}
\sum_{(i,j)\in M_r}
\left(y_{ij}-\widehat y_{ij}^{(-M_r)}\right)^2.
$$

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Let $O$ be the naturally observed cells and let $M_r\subset O$ be the cells hidden in mask replicate $r$. After fitting without $M_r$, the reconstruction of cell $(i,j)$ is $\widehat y_{ij}^{(-M_r)}$. Its mean squared reconstruction error is

$$
\operatorname{MSE}(M_r)
=\frac{1}{|M_r|}
\sum_{(i,j)\in M_r}
\left(y_{ij}-\widehat y_{ij}^{(-M_r)}\right)^2.
$$

[Sources]

Course note: missing-data/validating-imputation.qmd
:::

## Defining the validation error {.equation-slide}

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/validating-imputation/05-math; notes-page: missing-data/validating-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 57849066c62bd1fc5bd2959576cc380cafa4b3815fa7b03af158d050a6b793db; role: math -->

The superscript $(-M_r)$ records that the targets did not enter fitting. Because the acoustic columns have different scales, rank selection uses training-standardized error,

$$
\operatorname{RMSE}_{z}
=\sqrt{
  \frac{1}{\sum_r|M_r|}
  \sum_r\sum_{(i,j)\in M_r}
  \left(
    \frac{y_{ij}-\widehat y_{ij}^{(-M_r)}}
         {\widehat s_j^{(-M_r)}}
  \right)^2
},
$$

where $\widehat s_j^{(-M_r)}$ is estimated after masking.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The superscript $(-M_r)$ records that the targets did not enter fitting. Because the acoustic columns have different scales, rank selection uses training-standardized error,

$$

=\sqrt{

  \left(

         {\widehat s_j^{(-M_r)}}
  \right)^2
},
$$

where $\widehat s_j^{(-M_r)}$ is estimated after masking.

:::

## Recreating the disjoint masks

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/validating-imputation/08-concept; notes-page: missing-data/validating-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 57849066c62bd1fc5bd2959576cc380cafa4b3815fa7b03af158d050a6b793db; role: concept -->

Masks are created sequentially so that their targets are disjoint.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Seeds `20261018` through `20261025` identify eight validation masks, each hiding 5% of observed cells within every fallible column. Seeds `20261026` through `20261029` identify four test masks, each hiding 1.25% per fallible column. Masks are created sequentially so that their targets are disjoint.

The split contains 9,128 validation cells and 1,120 test cells.

## Selecting rank without test leakage

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/validating-imputation/10-concept; notes-page: missing-data/validating-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 57849066c62bd1fc5bd2959576cc380cafa4b3815fa7b03af158d050a6b793db; role: concept -->

No test value contributes to a validation prediction, a column center or scale, a component direction, or the selected rank.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The validation fits remove both the current validation mask and the entire test union. Thus no test value contributes to a validation prediction, a column center or scale, a component direction, or the selected rank.

## What this validation targets

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/validating-imputation/16-concept; notes-page: missing-data/validating-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 57849066c62bd1fc5bd2959576cc380cafa4b3815fa7b03af158d050a6b793db; role: concept -->

The results do not estimate prediction for a new speaker, a new vowel inventory, or a token with an entire contour absent.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

This is cell-level, transductive validation. The other measurements from the same token remain available because the intended use is to fill isolated F2 or F3 cells in an existing acoustic matrix. The results do not estimate prediction for a new speaker, a new vowel inventory, or a token with an entire contour absent.

[Sources]

Course note: missing-data/validating-imputation.qmd
:::

## What this validation targets

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/validating-imputation/17-concept; notes-page: missing-data/validating-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 57849066c62bd1fc5bd2959576cc380cafa4b3815fa7b03af158d050a6b793db; role: concept -->

It does not establish unbiased reconstruction of the 379 naturally missing cells.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

The masks are random within the 14 naturally fallible columns. They preserve the measurement columns but do not reproduce the observed dependence of natural missingness on vowel or value. Low test error thus supports interpolation under these registered masks. It does not establish unbiased reconstruction of the 379 naturally missing cells.

[Sources]

Course note: missing-data/validating-imputation.qmd
:::

## What this validation targets

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/validating-imputation/18-concept; notes-page: missing-data/validating-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 57849066c62bd1fc5bd2959576cc380cafa4b3815fa7b03af158d050a6b793db; role: concept -->

The calculation above prevents it by estimating every preprocessing quantity after masking and by excluding the test union throughout rank selection.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

Using the full matrix to calculate centers, scales, components, or rank would give held-out values an indirect path into their predictions. This is leakage through preprocessing. the calculation above prevents it by estimating every preprocessing quantity after masking and by excluding the test union throughout rank selection.

[Sources]

Course note: missing-data/validating-imputation.qmd
:::

## What this validation targets

<!-- generated-slide-id: missing-data/validating-imputation/19-concept; notes-page: missing-data/validating-imputation.qmd; note-sha256: 57849066c62bd1fc5bd2959576cc380cafa4b3815fa7b03af158d050a6b793db; role: concept -->

The prediction table retains token, vowel, formant, and measurement identifiers so those errors can be inspected at the level of a later linguistic claim.

::: {.notes}
[Transcript]

An overall error may still hide poor reconstruction for a vowel, speaker group, or measurement column. The prediction table retains token, vowel, formant, and measurement identifiers so those errors can be inspected at the level of a later linguistic claim.

[Sources]

Course note: missing-data/validating-imputation.qmd
:::

This result supports one cell-reconstruction target; it does not turn predictions for naturally missing cells into measurements.

Holdout validation by artificial masking evaluates an imputation procedure on observed values made unavailable during fitting.
